subject.title: fix(approvals): fail closed plugin tool gates

question: Should OpenClaw disable the shipped plugin `timeoutBehavior: "allow"` fallback in this release while retaining the field only as a deprecated no-op for one release train?
rationale: The implementation safely enforces fail-closed behavior, but the timing of an intentional shipped plugin API behavior change at an execution-authorization boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept fail-closed now
options.body: Ignore `timeoutBehavior: "allow"` immediately, warn once per plugin, and remove the field after the documented deprecation train.

options.title: Stage the cutover
options.body: Preserve allow-on-timeout temporarily and introduce a migration or explicit strict policy before removing the behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed now
recommendation.body: Ignore `timeoutBehavior: "allow"` immediately, warn once per plugin, and remove the field after the documented deprecation train.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the shared approval runtime and affected Codex, native-hook, and plugin consumers.
